protocol.name: D10 task-free multimodal response-curve pilot
protocol.purpose: test whether deterministic point-curve regression averages incompatible physical regimes and corrupts monitor geometry
protocol.scope: the same 218 fit groups and five episode-blocked folds as D9b; prior inspected TRAIN, DEV, and TEST remain closed

data.normalization: reuse each D9b fold's current-state, future-action, and response normalizers

model.input_and_backbone: unchanged D9b snapshot state, eight-step paired future controls, endpoint-symmetric pair encoder, and six-level context
model.distribution: one shared categorical latent for the complete six-level response group
model.per_mode_output: one nonnegative ReLU group amplitude times six level-specific softplus shapes
model.objective: categorical mixture of fixed-variance isotropic Gaussians over the complete 6-by-41 task-free log-response curve
model.fixed_sigma_reason: predeclared order-one normalized log-response scale; not selected using monitor decisions
model.deployment_readout: most probable component from input-conditioned categorical logits; never target-conditioned
model.diagnostic_only: oracle-best component MSE and component coverage; these cannot select deployment output

optimization.sampling: deterministic uniform group sampling without replacement; no class balancing
optimization.execution: one sequential GPU run at a time

decision.pass: replicate seeds 2 and 3 on the same fit-only folds before opening any held-out split
decision.fail_with_oracle_coverage_gain: mode inference is the bottleneck; test task-free latent routing without changing the monitor
decision.fail_without_oracle_coverage_gain: stop architecture iteration on this dataset; broaden generic physical interaction-response data or redesign the learned-model/monitor contract
